descriptionChirho: A perennial woody plant with a trunk and branches, used both literally of physical trees in nature and figuratively in parables and apocalyptic imagery. The singular and plural forms represent the same core botanical referent with no semantic differentiation. Multilingual glosses confirm uniform meaning across number: Spanish 'árbol/árboles,' Arabic 'شَجَرَة/الأَشْجَار,' Hindi 'पेड़/पेड़ों,' Korean '나무/나무들,' Swahili 'mti/miti.' NT occurrences include the parable of the fig tree (Matt 24:32; Mark 13:28; Luke 21:29), the tree known by its fruit (Matt 7:17-19; 12:33; Luke 6:43-44), Zacchaeus climbing a sycamore tree (Luke 19:4), and apocalyptic imagery of trees being burned (Rev 7:1, 3; 8:7; 9:4).
